title: fpqc covering of a scheme
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A family of morphisms of schemes $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ is an *fpqc covering* of $T$ if every $f_i$ is flat [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and for every affine open $V\subset T$ there are $n\ge0$, indices $i_1,\dots,i_n\in I$ and affine opens $V_j\subset T_{i_j}$ with $\bigcup_{j=1}^n f_{i_j}(V_j)=V$. (Then $T=\bigcup_i f_i(T_i)$, since $T$ is covered by affine opens.)

source.place: Stacks Project, Topologies, Definition topologies-definition-fpqc-covering (Tag 022B); used in Bhatt-Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, Definition 4.1.1, p. 27 (literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf)

mathlib_searches.verdict: match: Mathlib uses quasi-compact opens where Stacks uses affine opens; equivalent because an affine open is quasi-compact and a quasi-compact open is a finite union of affine opens; joint surjectivity, which Mathlib also requires, follows from the affine condition

mathlib_match.how: exact: a presieve is in `fpqcPrecoverage T` iff its arrows are flat, jointly surjective and form a `QuasiCompactCover` (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Cover/QuasiCompact.lean:38), whose condition with quasi-compact opens is equivalent to the Stacks condition with affine opens
